newsitem.title: UK: Northern says CE Electric bid too low.
newsitem.headline: Northern says CE Electric bid too low.

text.p: Northern Electric said on Friday it was confident it could demonstrate to shareholders that CE Electric's hostile bid for it at 630 pence was too low.
"There is nothing to talk about at this price," Northern Electric's chairman David Morris said in a statement.

The UK regional electricity group said it was disappointed that "speculation concerning a possible reference to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) of CE Electric's offers has depressed Northern Electric's share price, thereby enabling it to acquire shares in the market". Earlier CE Electric said it held 29.45 percent of the shares.
Shares in Northern Electric closed 19 pence lower at 604-1/2.
Northern Electric already rejected CE's estimated 650 million stg bid last week, arguing that it undervalued the company.
Analysts expected the regional electricity supplier to report glowing half-year results soon in an attempt to support its case that CE's bid was too low.
CE Electric is 70 percent owned by Nebraska-based CalEnergy, with the rest held by U.S. construction to telecoms group Peter Kiewit Sons.
